newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Feb. 4.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Feb. 4.

text.p: All major Mexican ports were open Tuesday as a new cold front approached the northern Gulf of Mexico, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in its 1000 local/1600 GMT daily report.
The cold front closed Tampico, Tuxpan, Veracruz and Nautla to smaller tourist and fishing boats, as winds in the region blew up to 35 kilometers.
Ships were advised of high winds and waves along the coasts of Tamaulipas and northern Veracruz states.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.
Scattered showers and clouds with maximum winds of 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 17 miles per hour) and waves from three to five feet high. -- Gulf of Mexico:
Cold front drawing winds from the north and northwest of 10 to 20 knots (19 to 38 km/11 to 22 miles per hour) along north and northeast of country.

Winds along northwest gulf clocked at 20 to 30 knots (38 to 56 km/22 to 34 miles per hour). Gusts of up to 40 knots (76 km/44 miles per hour) and waves from six to nine feet high moving south along the coast.
Partly cloudy and scattered rains with winds from the east at 20 to 30 km.
